title: Settlement Process
big_picture: If clearing works out the bill, settlement is the moment money and shares actually change hands: on T+1, members pay in by 11:00 am, money goes out at 1:30 pm and shares land in buyers' demat accounts by 3:30 pm. When a seller fails to deliver, the CC buys the shares in an auction or, failing that, closes out the deal at a penalty price. Derivatives settle daily through MTM and finally at expiry, in cash for indices and by delivery for stocks. When a company gives a bonus, split, rights or big dividend, F&O contracts are adjusted so nobody gains or loses from the event itself.
exam_focus: The T+1 clock: 7:30 am confirmation, 9:00 am obligations, 11:00 am pay-in, 1:30 pm funds pay-out, 3:30 pm direct securities pay-out; derivatives T+1 (currency T+2)
NEW: closing price is VWAP of the last 30 minutes now; the Closing Auction Session runs 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm in four 5-minute parts, with a random close, starting with F&O stocks
Funds rules: no cash, USCNBA/DSCNBA, running account conditions (30/90 days, 30 working days, 1 or 3 working days, 30 calendar days), 0.07% per day penal interest
Auction and close-out: timings, once only, within one week, Auction+1 settlement, 20% vs 10% close-out rules, Core SGF
Derivatives settlement: MTM, final settlement prices, exercise values, what long/short calls and puts turn into
Corporate actions: ex-date = record date under T+1, adjustment factors for bonus/split/rights, 2% dividend test, merger/demerger conditions

sections.title: Introduction: Settlement Cycles and the T+1 Day

blocks.text: Settlement once took a week; today all cash market trades settle on T+1: Monday's trades on Tuesday. A settlement cycle is the period within which settlement happens; when counting it, holidays are skipped: bank holidays, exchange/CC holidays, Saturdays and Sundays. An optional beta T+0 cycle runs alongside T+1.

items.title: Cash settlement (derivatives)
points: Only the price difference is paid

items.title: Physical settlement (derivatives)
points: The actual underlying security is delivered

blocks.text: Derivatives: daily and final settlement on T+1 working day, except final settlement of currency derivatives on T+2. Funds for daily MTM, cash-settled futures final settlement, premium and cash-settled options exercise move before market opens next day, around 8:30 am.

items: After holidays, several settlements may fall due together. CCs settle them sequentially: the first settlement's pay-in and pay-out finish before the next pay-in starts.

A strict schedule ensures all settlements finish the same day.

Funds pay-in = cumulative buy value; pay-out = cumulative sell value

sections.title: Closing Price and the new Closing Auction Session

blocks.text: Today: a stock's closing price in the equity cash segment is the Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) of trades in the last 30 minutes of the Continuous Trading Session (CTS).

Coming in: SEBI's circular dated January 16, 2026 introduces a Closing Auction Session (CAS) in the equity cash segment (with some changes to the pre-open auction session). It is phased in: first, stocks on which derivative contracts are available get their closing price from CAS.
CAS is a separate 20-minute session, 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm, on all trading days, in four 5-minute sub-sessions.

head: Sub-session
Starts
Duration
What happens
rows: Reference price calculation; transition from CTS to CAS
Order entry: both limit and market orders
Order entry for limit orders only; market orders cannot be modified/cancelled; random close in the last 2 minutes
blocks.caption: Closing Auction Session (NEW)

blocks.text: The random close stops anyone from timing a last-second order to nudge the price. Getting the close right matters because so much rests on it.

Importance of the closing price. It is the basis for: (1) the post-close session, (2) next day's base price, (3) next day's morning block deal window, (4) end-of-day index value, (5) settlement of derivatives contracts, (6) mark-to-market margin, (7) mutual fund NAV.
CAS in four 5-minute beats: Set (3:15 reference price), Enter all (3:20), Enter limits, random stop (3:25), Match (3:30), done by 3:35.
Today's method is VWAP of the last 30 minutes, not the last traded price. CAS lasts 20 minutes, and the random close is in the last 2 minutes of the third sub-session.

Every clearing member keeps a separate and distinct primary clearing account with a designated clearing bank, one per segment. Payers need clear funds by the stipulated pay-in time; banks debit/credit on CC instructions. Deposit in any form; withdraw only in self-name.

sections.title: Mode of Payment and Running Account Settlement

blocks.text: No cash, either way: not against obligations, not as margin, not against sales. Only account payee crossed cheque, demand draft, direct credit (NEFT etc.) or other RBI-approved modes, with cheques drawn by and issued to the client only. Members keep an audit trail showing electronic transfers and pre-funded instruments (pay order, DD, banker's cheque) came from the client's own bank account.

head: Account
Use

Receive client funds: "Name of the SB/CM - USCNB account"
Down Streaming Client Nodal Bank Account (DSCNBA)
Pay clients, only from here: "Name of the SB/CM - DSCNB account"
blocks.caption: Renamed by SEBI circular of December 13, 2023 (earlier "Name of Stock Broker - Client Account")

blocks.text: Upstream: money comes up from the client. Downstream: money goes down to the client.

Default: client funds settled within 24 hours / 1 working day of pay-out, unless the client authorises a running account, now for funds only (securities running account discontinued, SEBI circular June 20, 2019).

Detail

Monthly or quarterly per client choice: at least once in 30 / 90 days, on EOD obligation across all exchanges
First Friday and/or Saturday of the month/quarter, per the annual calendar exchanges jointly issue at the start of the financial year
Funds ledger and securities register extracts; disputes within 30 working days
Funds for outstanding obligations may be retained as SEBI/exchanges specify
Electronic; physical instrument only if electronic payment fails
Within 1 working day if with broker; 3 working days if with CM/CC
No trade in 30 calendar days: entire credit balance returned on the next monthly settlement date, whatever the preference (unless he trades before it)
No inter-client adjustment; funds from a settled client stay in the USCNBA
MTF funds/securities; BG/FDR collateral; institutional clients settling via custodians

items: An Authorised Person may not accept client funds or securities, and trades proprietarily only with his own money.
SEBI (June 2025) mandated validated, exclusive UPI IDs for SEBI-registered intermediaries collecting investor funds.

blocks.text: Dispute window: 30 working days. Inactivity trigger: 30 calendar days. The inactive client is paid on the monthly date even if he chose quarterly.
CMs and custodians pay the clearing agency what they owe for each settlement, and the agency pays them what is due, based on exchange/clearing agency data.
Missing a funds obligation (including STT/stamp duty, Capital Cushion and valuation debits) can mean withdrawal of trading facility and disciplinary action.

items: Trading facility withdrawn and securities pay-out withheld if the shortfall exceeds the SEBI/CC limit, or shortages recur within a set period and amount.
Penal interest of not less than 0.07% per day on the shortage.
If the defaulter never brings the funds within the allowed time, the CC may close out securities in the normal or auction market.

blocks.title: Cost of being short
blocks.text: Short by ₹10,00,000 at pay-in: penal interest of at least ₹700 per day.
Demat deliveries go directly to/from clients' beneficiary accounts (except to entities under approved schemes). With direct pay-out, buyers get shares on settlement day by 3:30 pm.

items: Seller: on learning of execution, gives a delivery (debit) instruction to his DP to move shares to the broker's pool account, or lets the broker do it under DDPI.
Buyer: a one-time standing instruction to the DP (at opening or later), or a receipt instruction for each purchase.
Block mechanism and pay-in validation apply (5.6.2, 5.6.3).

sections.title: Settlement through the Depository Clearing System

blocks.text: Securities pay-in is on T+0 and/or T+1 by cycle. Members keep settlement (pool) accounts with both NSDL and CDSL, mandatory even if pay-out is taken in a preferred depository. TMs clearing through another CM also need TM pool accounts in both.

blocks.text: Physical settlement of F&O (SEBI, November 30, 2022): obligations are netted with Capital Market obligations of the same trade date where CM-TM-client (UCC) and security match, and settled in the CM segment's settlement type and number.

A seller who fails to deliver is penalised; the shortage value counts as a funds shortage if the clearing bank does not confirm it. Shortages arise when a short seller fails to square up, delivery is late, or shares are bad/wrong. The member is debited the undelivered shares' value at a valuation price: the valuation debit. To honour the buyer, the CC runs a buy-in auction through the exchange on settlement day and delivers the shares bought.

blocks.text: If one client of a broker fails to deliver while another client bought the same quantity, netting leaves the broker with no CC obligation, yet the buyer gets nothing: an internal shortage.

items: Members report internal shortages on pay-in day for a self-auction; the CC clubs them with normal shortages in one auction.
With direct pay-out, SEBI asked TMs/CMs to use the CC auction for such shortages and charge clients nothing beyond CC charges.
If the CC cannot get the shares, the member closes out per CC guidelines.
CCs may charge fees and may not give settlement guarantee for these auctions.

blocks.title: Internal shortage
blocks.text: Client A sells and client B buys 50 shares of X through broker K, so K's net obligation is nil. A fails to deliver; K reports 50 shares for self-auction on pay-in day.
If the auction finds no sellers, the CC closes out: the defaulter is charged a close-out price and the buyer is compensated in money. Some shortages go straight to close-out.

head: Situation
Close-out price (whichever is higher)
rows: Highest price across exchanges from trade day till auction day, OR 20% above official closing (settlement) price on auction day
Corporate action: cum-basis shortage whose auction pay-out cannot happen by Record Date/Book Closure minus 1 business day
Highest price across exchanges from trade day till auction day, OR 10% above settlement price on auction day (or as declared)
Highest price across exchanges on T day (till settlement minus 1 day), OR 20% above settlement price on T day
10% above the day's highest price across all exchanges
Auction seller fails on auction pay-in day
Highest price from original trade day till auction day, OR 20% above closing price on close-out day; charged to the auction seller

blocks.text: For corporate actions, cum-basis shortages go to auction only if auction pay-out is on or before Record Date/Book Closure minus 1 business day; otherwise they are closed out directly.

blocks.title: Close-out
blocks.text: 100 shares undelivered, no auction offers. Highest price, trade day to auction day: ₹540. Auction-day close ₹480, plus 20% = ₹576. Higher is ₹576: seller charged ₹57,600.
Proceeds settle the aggrieved party's claim; any balance goes to the Core Settlement Guarantee Fund (Core SGF), not to the defaulter.
20% is the normal mark-up; 10% is for corporate-action cum shortages and T+0 (in T+0, 10% above the day's highest price).
Since October 2019, stock futures and options open at expiry are physically settled; index F&O remain cash-settled.

Futures settle (A) daily by mark-to-market (MTM): the loser's CM pays, the gainer's CM receives, and positions are reset to the daily settlement price; MTM is always cash. CMs collect/settle MTM for their TMs and clients. (B) Final settlement happens on the last trading day.

blocks.text: Options: (A) daily premium: buyer pays, seller receives, netted per client per contract. (B) Final exercise: all ITM stock options are auto-exercised on expiry. Index options are European (exercise on expiry only); ITM longs are randomly assigned to shorts of the same series. Final settlement price = underlying's closing price on expiry.
Exercise value per unit: Call = closing price - strike; Put = strike - closing price.

Results in
blocks.caption: Obligation valued at the option's strike price

blocks.title: Two expiries
blocks.text:
Index put, strike ₹22,000, index closes ₹21,700, 75 units: long gets 300 x 75 = ₹22,500 cash.
Stock call, strike ₹1,400, stock closes ₹1,450, lot 500: long receives 500 shares and pays ₹7,00,000 (strike x 500).
Long call = you call the shares in (buy). Long put = you put them out (sell). Shorts do the opposite.
Daily settlement price: the contract's closing price (on an exchange or across exchanges); for illiquid contracts, a theoretical price per SEBI guidelines.

blocks.text: Funds (6.6.2): MTM, cash-settled futures final settlement, premium and cash-settled exercise obligations are netted at CM level; pay-in before market hours next day, pay-out credited after, as in the cash market.

Securities (6.6.3): a CM's deliverable/receivable positions are netted across all its clients/TMs. On stock derivative expiry, cash and physical F&O obligations are settled net (Box 5.1) in the CM segment's settlement type and number.

sections.title: Corporate Actions: Record Date and Ex-Date

blocks.text: Corporate actions (rights, bonus, split, dividend) go to those holding shares on the record date. A stock trades cum-benefit up to 1 trading day before the record date; the day it trades without the benefit is the ex-date, from which exchanges adjust the base price.

blocks.title: Who gets the bonus?
blocks.text: Bought May 27: shares arrive May 28 (T+1) before EOD, so eligible. Bought May 28: shares arrive May 29, not eligible.
Under T+1, ex-date = record date. Record date December 22 means ex-date December 22.

sections.title: Corporate Actions to be Adjusted, Timing and What Changes

blocks.text: Bonus, rights, extraordinary dividends, mergers/demergers, amalgamation, splits and consolidations alter F&O contracts. Principle: keep the value of positions the same on cum and ex dates as far as possible, preserving ITM/ATM/OTM status and smooth exercise/assignment.

When (6.7.3): on the last cum day, after trading closes. What (6.7.4): strike price, position, market lot/multiplier, on all open positions. Expiry may also change: contracts force-closed and replaced by adjusted ones.

head: Item
Bonus / split / consolidation
rows: Bonus A:B: (A+B)/B. Split or consolidation A:B: A/B

blocks.title: Bonus 1:1
blocks.text: AF = 2. Strike ₹500 becomes ₹250; lot 1,000 becomes 2,000; a 2,000-share position becomes 4,000. Value stays ₹10,00,000.

blocks.title: Split and consolidation
blocks.text:
Split 5:1 (one ₹10 share into five ₹2 shares): AF = 5. Strike ₹2,000 becomes ₹400; lot 250 becomes 1,250.
Consolidation 1:10: AF = 0.1. Strike ₹20 becomes ₹200; lot 10,000 becomes 1,000.
More, cheaper shares: bonus and split divide the strike and multiply lot and position.

Rights work the other way: strike x AF; lot and position ÷ AF. With A = rights entitlement, B = existing shares, P = close on last cum date, S = issue price: benefit per entitlement = (P - S) x A; benefit per share E = (P - S) x A / (A + B); AF = (P - E) / P. Any dividend declared with the rights follows the dividend policy.

blocks.title: Rights 1:4
blocks.text: P = ₹200, S = ₹100: E = 100 x 1/5 = ₹20; AF = 180/200 = 0.9. Strike ₹220 becomes ₹198; lot 900 becomes 1,000. Value unchanged at ₹1,98,000.

Fractions (e.g. bonus 3:7): (1) value the position before; (2) value with the exact AF; (3) round strike to nearest tick, lot to nearest integer; (4) revalue. The relevant authority covers the gap between 1 and 4 by adjusting strike or lot, without forced closure.

blocks.title: Bonus 3:7
blocks.text: AF = 10/7. Strike ₹1,000 becomes ₹700; lot 400 becomes 571.43, rounded to 571. Value ₹4,00,000 before, ₹3,99,700 after rounding: the ₹300 gap is fixed by tweaking strike or lot.

head: Dividend
F&O adjustment
rows: At or above 2% (extraordinary), or any dividend where the company sought exemption from SEBI LODR (2015) timelines

items: Market price for the 2% test: close on the day before the board announces; if announced after market hours, that same day's close. If the AGM changes the rate: the post-AGM rate and the close on the day before the AGM.
Extraordinary: the total dividend (special and/or ordinary) is reduced from all option strikes from the ex-dividend date; futures carry forward at daily settlement price less the dividend.

blocks.title: 2% test
blocks.text: Close ₹1,000 the day before the board meeting. Dividend ₹15 (1.5%): no change. Dividend ₹25 (2.5%): a ₹1,000 call becomes a ₹975 call; futures carry forward at settlement price minus ₹25.

items: Merger: when the record date is announced, members are told the expiry (last cum-date); no fresh contracts on a stock that will cease to exist; unexpired contracts are compulsorily settled at the underlying's close on the last cum-date.

blocks.text: Demerger: derivatives can be re-introduced on the post-restructured company from its first listing day only if all hold: (a) F&O on the original company traded before restructuring; (b) its market cap was at least ₹1,000 crore; (c) the new company is likely to be at least one-third its size by revenue, assets or analyst valuation; (d) nothing (e.g. extremely low free float) makes it ineligible.
If met: existing contracts expire on the last cum date; near, middle and far month contracts on the restructured company start from the demerger ex-date.
Other corporate actions are adjusted case by case by the relevant authority on the same principles, including compulsory close-out where needed.

flashcards.q: What is a settlement cycle?
flashcards.a: The period within which settlement is made; for cash equities it is T+1, excluding holidays and weekends.

flashcards.q: Cash settlement vs physical settlement of derivatives?
flashcards.a: Cash: only the price difference is paid. Physical: the underlying security is delivered.

flashcards.q: Which equity derivatives are cash-settled and which physical?
flashcards.a: Index F&O: cash. Stock F&O: physical (since October 2019).

flashcards.q: When is the final settlement of currency derivatives?
flashcards.a: T+2 (expiry + 2 days); other derivatives settle on T+1.

flashcards.q: When is securities pay-out under direct pay-out?
flashcards.a: By 3:30 pm on T+1, straight into the client's demat account.

flashcards.q: Holiday settlement rule?
flashcards.a: Sequential: first settlement's pay-in and pay-out complete before the next; inter-depository transfers within one hour.

flashcards.q: Gross (trade-to-trade) obligation for securities?
flashcards.a: Pay-in = cumulative sell quantity; pay-out = cumulative buy quantity; no netting.

flashcards.q: How is the closing price computed today?
flashcards.a: VWAP of trades in the last 30 minutes of the continuous trading session.

flashcards.q: What is CAS and its timing?
flashcards.a: Closing Auction Session (SEBI, Jan 16, 2026): 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm, four 5-minute sub-sessions.

flashcards.q: Which stocks get CAS first?
flashcards.a: Stocks on which derivative contracts are available.

flashcards.q: When is the random close in CAS?
flashcards.a: In the last 2 minutes of the 3:25 pm sub-session (limit orders only).

flashcards.q: Name four uses of the closing price.
flashcards.a: Next day's base price, end-of-day index value, derivatives settlement, MTM margin (also MF NAV, post-close, block window).

flashcards.q: USCNBA vs DSCNBA?
flashcards.a: USCNBA receives client funds; DSCNBA is the only account for paying clients.

flashcards.q: Can a broker accept cash from a client?
flashcards.a: No. Only account payee cheques, DDs, NEFT/direct credit or other RBI-approved modes.

flashcards.q: Who may sign a running account authorisation?
flashcards.a: Only the client; not an Authorised Person or PoA holder.

flashcards.q: Running account settlement dates?
flashcards.a: First Friday and/or Saturday of the month or quarter, per the exchanges' annual calendar.

flashcards.q: Dispute window for running account statements?
flashcards.a: 30 working days from the statement date.

flashcards.q: Inactive client rule?
flashcards.a: No trade for 30 calendar days: full credit balance returned on the next monthly settlement date.

flashcards.q: Penal interest on funds shortage?
flashcards.a: Not less than 0.07% per day.

flashcards.q: What is a valuation debit?
flashcards.a: Debit to a member for undelivered securities, valued at the valuation price.

flashcards.q: Auction timing on NSE and BSE?
flashcards.a: Settlement day after pay-out: NSE 2:30 pm onwards; BSE 2:00 to 2:45 pm.

flashcards.q: Auction pay-in and pay-out day?
flashcards.a: Auction + 1 day.

flashcards.q: What is an internal shortage?
flashcards.a: A client fails to deliver but the broker's net obligation was nil because another client bought; handled by self-auction.

flashcards.q: Normal close-out price?
flashcards.a: Higher of highest price from trade day to auction day, or 20% above closing price on auction day.

flashcards.q: Where does surplus from auction/close-out go?
flashcards.a: To the Core Settlement Guarantee Fund, not the defaulter.

flashcards.q: Exercise value of a call and a put?
flashcards.a: Call = closing price - strike; Put = strike - closing price.

flashcards.q: Long put exercised in a physically settled stock option results in?
flashcards.a: A sell position: deliver shares, valued at strike price.

flashcards.q: Final settlement price for stock F&O?
flashcards.a: Closing price of the stock in the CM segment across exchanges on the last trading day.

flashcards.q: Exercise style of index options in India?
flashcards.a: European: exercised only on expiry day; ITM longs randomly assigned to shorts of the same series.

flashcards.q: Under T+1, how do ex-date and record date relate?
flashcards.a: They are the same day.

flashcards.q: When are corporate action adjustments made in F&O?
flashcards.a: On the last cum day, after close of trading, on all open positions.

flashcards.q: Bonus A:B adjustment factor and effect?
flashcards.a: (A+B)/B; strike divided by it, lot and position multiplied by it.

flashcards.q: Rights adjustment factor?
flashcards.a: (P-E)/P with E = (P-S)A/(A+B); strike multiplied, lot and position divided.

flashcards.q: When is a dividend extraordinary for F&O?
flashcards.a: At or above 2% of market value (or LODR timeline exemption sought).

flashcards.q: Demerger: two size tests for re-introducing derivatives?
flashcards.a: Pre-restructured market cap at least ₹1,000 crore; new company at least one-third its size.

questions.q: After receiving intimation from his broker that his sale has been executed, what kind of instruction should the client give to his DP?
questions.why: The seller issues a delivery instruction slip, i.e. a debit instruction, to move shares from his demat account to the broker's pool account.

questions.q: Corporate action adjustments in equity F&O are carried out on all ........ positions.
questions.why: Adjustments for corporate actions are made on all open positions.

questions.q: What does the clearing corporation do when a broker fails to deliver securities?
questions.why: For delivery shortages the CC conducts a buy-in auction to buy shares from the market for the buying broker.

questions.q: When a company declares an extraordinary dividend, the total dividend amount is ........ all strike prices of option contracts on that stock.
questions.why: For extraordinary dividends the total dividend is reduced from all strike prices from the ex-dividend date.

questions.q: For computing the end-of-day index value, which price of the constituent shares is used?
questions.why: The closing price is the basis for computing the end-of-day index value.

questions.q: Brokers must not accept ........ from clients, whether against obligations or as margin.
questions.why: Cash is prohibited; payments must be by account payee cheque, DD, direct credit or other RBI-approved modes.

questions.q: If a company's record date is December 22, 202X, what is the ex-date in the equity segment under T+1 settlement?
questions.why: Under T+1 a stock trades cum-benefit until 1 trading day before the record date, so the ex-date is the record date itself.

questions.q: Final settlement of currency derivatives takes place on expiry plus how many days?
questions.why: Currency derivatives' final settlement is on T+2; other derivatives settle on T+1.

questions.q: How is the closing price of a stock in the equity cash segment currently determined?
options: VWAP of trades in the last 30 minutes of the continuous trading session
Simple average of the last 30 trades
VWAP of the whole trading day
questions.why: Currently the closing price is the VWAP of trades in the last thirty minutes of the CTS.

questions.q: Under SEBI's January 16, 2026 circular, the Closing Auction Session (CAS) runs:
questions.why: CAS is a separate 20-minute session from 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm on all trading days.

questions.q: In the Closing Auction Session, the random close happens:
options: During reference price calculation at 3:15 pm
During order entry for both limit and market orders at 3:20 pm
In the last 2 minutes of the order-entry period starting 3:25 pm
questions.why: The third sub-session (3:25 pm) allows limit orders only and ends with a random close in the last 2 minutes.

questions.q: In the initial phase, the closing price of which stocks will be determined through the Closing Auction Session?
options: Stocks on which derivative contracts are available
questions.why: CAS is phased in, starting with cash segment stocks on which derivative contracts are available.

questions.q: What is permitted in the CAS sub-session starting at 3:25 pm?
options: Order entry for limit orders; market orders cannot be modified or cancelled
Entry of both limit and market orders
questions.why: From 3:25 pm only limit orders can be entered, market orders cannot be modified/cancelled, and the session closes randomly in the last 2 minutes.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed in the workbook as a use of the closing price?
options: Fixing the issue price in an IPO
questions.why: The closing price feeds the post-close session, base price, block window, index value, derivatives settlement, MTM and MF NAV, not IPO pricing.

questions.q: When several settlements fall due together after holidays, depositories must complete inter-depository transfers:
options: Within one hour and before the next settlement's pay-in begins
questions.why: Depositories must facilitate inter-depository transfers within one hour and before pay-in for the subsequent settlement.

questions.q: Under trade-to-trade (gross) settlement, a member's securities pay-in obligation equals:
questions.why: With no netting, securities pay-in equals the cumulative sell quantity and pay-out the cumulative buy quantity.

questions.q: The penal interest an exchange/CC may levy on a member's funds pay-in shortage is:
questions.why: Penal interest of not less than 0.07 percent per day may be levied on the pay-in shortage.

questions.q: Within how many days must a client raise a dispute about a running account statement?
questions.why: Disputes must be brought to the broker's notice within 30 working days from the statement date.

questions.q: A client who opted for quarterly running account settlement has a credit balance and has not traded for 30 calendar days. The broker must:
options: Wait for the next quarterly settlement
Return the entire credit balance on the upcoming monthly settlement date
Transfer it to the Investor Protection Fund
questions.why: Inactive clients' balances are returned on the next monthly settlement date irrespective of their preferred cycle.

questions.q: A client asks for funds lying with the clearing member/clearing corporation. Within how long must the stock broker transfer them?
questions.why: Within 1 working day if lying with the broker; within 3 working days if lying with the CM/CC.

questions.q: A running account authorisation may be signed by:
options: The Authorised Person of the broker
questions.why: The authorisation must be signed by the client only, not by an AP or PoA holder, and must be dated and revocable.

questions.q: How many categories of demat accounts are stock brokers permitted to maintain as specified by SEBI?
questions.why: Proprietary, pool, client unpaid securities pledgee, client securities margin pledge, client securities under funding, and client nodal MFOS: six.

questions.q: On NSE, the auction for undelivered quantities is conducted on settlement day:
questions.why: NSE auctions run from 2:30 pm onwards after pay-out; BSE's window is 2:00 pm to 2:45 pm.

questions.q: An auction for a shortage can in no case be held beyond:
options: One week from the pay-in day of the settlement
Three days from the trade date
One month from the trade date
questions.why: No auction may be held beyond one week from the pay-in day of the relevant settlement.

questions.q: If no sellers come forward in the auction, the shortage is closed out at:
options: The higher of the highest price from trade day till auction day, or 20% above the official closing price on auction day
questions.why: Normal close-out uses the higher of the highest price across exchanges till auction day or 20% above the auction-day closing price.

questions.q: Shortages in block deal window and trade-for-trade trades are directly closed out at the higher of the highest price on T day or:
options: 20% above the settlement price on T day
10% above the settlement price on T day
questions.why: Block window and TFT shortages go straight to close-out at the higher of the T-day highest price or 20% above the T-day settlement price.

questions.q: A seller fails to deliver 100 shares; the auction draws no offers. The highest price from trade day to auction day is ₹540 and the closing price on auction day is ₹480. What is the close-out amount?
questions.why: 20% above ₹480 is ₹576, which is higher than ₹540, so 100 x ₹576 = ₹57,600.

questions.q: Any amount left over from auction or close-out proceeds after settling the aggrieved party's claim is credited to:
questions.why: The balance goes to the Core SGF instead of the defaulting party's account.

questions.q: An investor buys one lot (200 units) of an index future at ₹2,502. The final settlement price on expiry is ₹2,545. What is the total MTM profit received over the contract's life?
questions.why: Net MTM = (2,545 - 2,502) x 200 = ₹8,600, paid out through daily MTM and final settlement.

questions.q: In a physically settled stock option, exercise of a long call results in:
questions.why: Exercise of a long call creates a buy (receivable) position; assignment of a short call creates a sell position.

questions.q: In a physically settled stock option, assignment of a short put results in:
questions.why: The assigned put writer must buy the shares: a buy (receivable) position at the strike price.

questions.q: A stock announces a 2:1 bonus (2 new shares for every 1 held). An option has strike ₹900 and market lot 300. What are the adjusted strike and lot?
questions.why: Adjustment factor = (2+1)/1 = 3; strike ₹900 / 3 = ₹300; lot 300 x 3 = 900.

questions.q: A rights issue has P = ₹200, S = ₹100 and ratio 1:4 (A = 1, B = 4). What is the adjustment factor?
questions.why: E = (200 - 100) x 1/5 = ₹20; AF = (200 - 20)/200 = 0.9. Strike is multiplied and lot divided by 0.9.

questions.q: For equity F&O adjustment, a dividend is treated as extraordinary when it is at or above what share of the market value of the stock?
questions.why: Dividends below 2% are ordinary and need no adjustment; at or above 2% they are extraordinary.

questions.q: A board announces a dividend after market hours on the 10th. For the 2% test, which market price is used?
options: Average price of the past month
questions.why: If the announcement comes after market hours, the same day's closing price is the market price.

questions.q: To re-introduce derivatives on a demerged company, the pre-restructured company must have had a market capitalisation of at least:
questions.why: One condition is a pre-restructuring market cap of at least ₹1,000 crore; the new company must also be at least one-third its size.

questions.q: Corporate action adjustments in equity F&O are carried out on the last cum day, after the close of trading hours.
questions.why: Adjustments are made on the last day the security trades cum-benefit in the cash market, after trading hours.

questions.q: The clearing corporation always provides settlement guarantee for auctions of internal shortages.
questions.why: CCs may charge fees for internal shortage auctions and may not provide settlement guarantee for them.
